_about: Every number the pipeline uses lives here, with where it came from. 'verified' = read in an official source (HCD/statute). 'secondary' = law-firm or city summary; confirm against the HCD fact sheet or statute before relying on it. 'assumed' = team assumption, label it in the demo.

SB684_SB1123.name: SB 684 / SB 1123 starter homes
SB684_SB1123.plain: Split into up to 10 small ownership lots, approved without a hearing
SB684_SB1123.notes: Gov Code 66499.41 (as amended 2025): 10 or fewer parcels and units; multifamily-zoned lot up to 5 acres, or vacant single-family lot up to 1.5 acres, substantially surrounded by urban uses. New parcels at least 600 sq ft (multifamily) or 1,200 sq ft (single-family). Excludes very high fire hazard zones and other SB 35 site exclusions.

SB9.name: SB 9 lot split + duplex
SB9.plain: Split a single-family lot in two and build two homes on each
SB9.notes: Single-family zones only. Each new lot at least 1,200 sq ft and at least 40% of the original. Very high fire hazard zones, special flood hazard areas and earthquake fault zones are allowed only with mitigation. Excluded: historic districts, housing occupied by tenants in the last 3 years, Ellis Act withdrawals in the last 15 years. Gov Code 65852.21, 66411.7.

AB2011_100.name: AB 2011, 100% affordable
AB2011_100.plain: All-affordable housing on commercially zoned land, approved without rezoning
AB2011_100.notes: Metropolitan jurisdictions: at least 30 units/acre, or local density if higher. Gov Code 65912.110-114. Site tests: not next to heavy industry, SB 35 environmental exclusions (fire, flood, etc.).

AB2011_MIXED.name: AB 2011, mixed-income on a commercial corridor
AB2011_MIXED.plain: Market-rate plus affordable homes on a commercial street, for sale or rent, no hearing
AB2011_MIXED.ownership_affordability: For-sale projects: 30% of homes for moderate income or 15% for lower income, deed-restricted 45 years
AB2011_MIXED.notes: Gov Code 65912.123(c)(1), metropolitan jurisdictions: greater of local density or 30/acre (<1 acre), 40/acre (1+ acre, corridor <100 ft), 60/acre (1+ acre, corridor 100+ ft), 80/acre (within 1/2 mile of a major transit stop). Non-metro numbers are lower (20/30/50/70). Site must front a commercial corridor 70-150 ft wide.

SB4.name: SB 4 faith & college land
SB4.plain: Affordable housing by right on land owned by a congregation or nonprofit college
SB4.notes: HCD fact sheet (April 2026): 30 units/acre in a metropolitan county (Orange County), 40 units/acre in zones that don't allow housing. Only applies when the owner is a religious institution or nonprofit college: needs owner data (not in free parcel layers).

HOUSING_ELEMENT.name: City's own Housing Element listing
HOUSING_ELEMENT.plain: The city already told the state this site can hold these homes
HOUSING_ELEMENT.notes: Capacity by income level as listed in the adopted 6th-cycle Housing Element site inventory (SCAG regional copy). A site the city listed is one it has to keep zoned for that capacity.

BASE_ZONING.name: Current zoning
BASE_ZONING.plain: What the city's zoning already allows
BASE_ZONING.notes: Fill zone_density below from the Santa Ana zoning code (units per acre per zone).

zone_code_classes._note: Santa Ana zone codes (SCAG ZN24_CITY) mapped to the tool's categories. Assumed from the code names; check against the Santa Ana zoning ordinance. Regex, matched in order.

zone_density._note: Units per acre by zone code. Empty until the team adds them from the city zoning code. Example shape: {"R2": 15}

surplus_land.notes: Housing sponsors get 60 days to respond to a notice, then 90 days of good-faith negotiation. If nobody responds or talks fail, the agency may sell to anyone, but residential projects of 10+ homes on that land must keep 15% affordable. Agencies are not required to sell below market value (Santa Ana staff report, Oct 2023).

people.notes: Placeholder mix for ownership townhomes. Replace with a real project's mix later.

pressure.notes: Lower-income progress = (very-low + low income homes built) / (very-low + low RHNA). Pressure compares that with the share of the 8-year cycle already elapsed.

land_use_candidates._note: SCAG existing land use codes (2024) that make a parcel a candidate. Codes from SCAG's land use code legend.

aerial._note: Aerial view settings. Photos: USDA NAIP via USGS (public domain). Usable area = parcel minus a setback strip minus existing buildings (OC Building Footprints) plus clearance.
aerial.notes: Setback and clearance are simple placeholders, not the city's development standards. Icons show how many homes the legal pathway allows spread over the open part of the lot; they are not a site plan.
